title: Trump eases Russia sanctions for diesel
ticker: BREAKING: U.S. suspends sanctions on Russian diesel after Trump-Putin call
Treasury's General License 135 runs until April 7, 2027
Trump: Russia to release over 300,000 tons of diesel immediately
Zelensky calls the deal "not fair and not honest"
EU and UK bans on Russian fuel remain in force

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tonight, a major reversal in Washington. President Trump has *suspended U.S. sanctions* on Russian diesel.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The move follows a phone call with Vladimir Putin, and comes just weeks after the president signed one of the *toughest Russia sanctions laws* in years.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Coming up: what exactly was agreed, why the White House says it's about *fuel prices*, and why Ukraine is calling it a betrayal.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Plus, the backlash from *both parties* in Congress.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We begin with that phone call.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Thursday, President Trump spoke by phone with Russian President *Vladimir Putin*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Shortly after, the president announced a deal. Russia, he said, would release large amounts of diesel fuel onto *world markets*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: To make that possible, the United States would set aside its own sanctions on Russian diesel.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Within hours, the Treasury Department's sanctions office issued what's called *General License 135*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It authorizes the sale, delivery and import of Russian origin diesel, until *April seventh, 2027*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: President Trump said he was happy with the deal. Putin's own statement gave *no specifics* on timing or volume.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Here is the schedule the president laid out on social media.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: More than *three hundred thousand tons* right away, another five hundred thousand tons in November, and one million tons after that.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Roughly three million more tons would follow later, for a total of up to *4.8 million tons*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The later shipments depend on how much Russia's refineries can actually produce.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: So why make this deal now? The answer, the White House says, is *the price at the pump*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: U.S. diesel hit a national average record of about *six dollars and twenty nine cents* a gallon in mid September, according to government data.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: That figure comes from the U.S. *Energy Information Administration*. Private trackers put the peak even higher, around six dollars and forty cents.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: As of this week, prices were still only around *twenty cents* below that record.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The spike is tied to the *war with Iran*. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year caused what analysts call the largest oil supply shock ever recorded.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Shipping through the strait has improved in recent weeks, but fuel prices have stayed stubbornly high.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And with the *midterm elections* less than a month away, high diesel prices are hurting truckers, farmers and voters alike.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The president has argued that more supply will push prices down *quickly*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But this deal comes as a surprise, because only weeks ago, the president was moving in the *opposite direction*.

scenes.title: FROM TOUGH SANCTIONS TO A WAIVER

items.text: Senate passes Graham sanctions bill, 86 votes

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The bill was the signature cause of Senator *Lindsey Graham*, who died in July.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Graham first pushed the idea in 2025, originally proposing tariffs as high as *five hundred percent* on buyers of Russian energy.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It passed the Senate in August with eighty six votes, and the House in September, *two sixty two to one fifty nine*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On September eighteenth, President Trump signed it into law as the *Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The law targets Russian officials, banks, oligarchs and the so called *shadow fleet* of oil tankers.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It also lets the president impose tariffs of up to *one hundred percent* on countries that buy Russian oil and gas.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The same law extends U.S. sanctions on *Iran* for another five years.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Three weeks later, the administration is now opening the door to Russian diesel *instead*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Legal experts note that the license does not repeal the *import ban* Congress passed in 2022, and some say the deal contradicts sanctions law.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The sharpest reaction came from Kyiv.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios the deal was *not fair and not honest*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He called it a *gift to Putin*, and warned it would give the Kremlin more money to fund its war against Ukraine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In a statement, he said any easing of sanctions without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement is an *obvious weakness*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The two leaders had already clashed over diesel. Last month, the president urged Ukraine to stop striking *Russian refineries*, saying the attacks were hurting the whole world.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On September thirteenth, the president said publicly, there are plenty of other targets. *Don't strike diesel*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: According to Axios, he repeated that request in a *phone call* with Zelensky a week later.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Asked about Zelensky's criticism this week, President Trump declined to respond directly. The Hill reported that he said Ukraine should *get a new leader*.

scenes.name: Europe
scenes.quote: EU and UK import bans on Russian fuel, and the $100 per barrel price cap on Russian products, remain in force.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In Europe, the German government *condemned* the agreement, and reaffirmed its commitment to EU sanctions on Russia.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Importantly, the American license does not change *European rules*. EU and British import bans on Russian fuel remain fully in force.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Back in Washington, the criticism is coming from *both sides* of the aisle.

scenes.name: Shaheen · Schumer · Warren
scenes.quote: A total betrayal of Ukraine, our European allies and American national security.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In a joint statement, Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Chuck Schumer and Elizabeth Warren called the move a *total betrayal* of Ukraine, America's European allies and U.S. national security.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Senator Richard Blumenthal, who co-wrote the sanctions law with Graham, urged the president to *rescind this agreement immediately*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Senator Mark Kelly put it more simply. *Whose side is Trump on?*

scenes.name: Lisa Murkowski
scenes.quote: ...instead of allowing Russia to export diesel, rake in revenues, and continue its catastrophic war in Ukraine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Republicans pushed back too. Senator Lisa Murkowski said the president should use the sanctions powers Congress just passed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Instead, she said, the deal allows Russia to export diesel, *rake in revenues*, and continue its catastrophic war in Ukraine.

scenes.name: Don Bacon
scenes.quote: Propping up Russia's war economy is terrible.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Republican Congressman Don Bacon said the president has always had a *moral blindness* when it comes to Putin.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Propping up Russia's war economy, he said, *is terrible*.

scenes.name: Mike Pence
scenes.quote: Makes no sense and is a betrayal of the legacy and leadership of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Even the president's former vice president weighed in. Mike Pence said lifting sanctions on Russian fuel while Putin attacks civilian targets in Ukraine *makes no sense*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He called it a *betrayal* of the legacy of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So the big question now: will Russian diesel actually bring prices down, and what does it cost Washington's *credibility* on sanctions?

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Our reporter has more.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: So will the deal actually bring prices down? Many analysts are *skeptical*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The world uses around *thirty million barrels* of diesel every day. One analyst told Al Jazeera the Russian shipments are only a short term fix.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For now, the license runs for *six months*, through early April.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The White House is betting cheaper fuel will matter more to voters than the backlash. Whether that bet pays off may be clear by *Election Day*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Reporting from Washington, for KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: To recap tonight's top story.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: After a call with Vladimir Putin, President Trump has suspended U.S. sanctions on *Russian diesel* until April 2027.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The White House says the goal is to bring down near record *fuel prices* before the midterms.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Ukraine calls the deal a *gift to Putin*, Germany has condemned it, and lawmakers from both parties are demanding it be reversed.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: All this, just three weeks after the president signed a sweeping new *Russia sanctions law*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll be following what happens next. That's all for tonight. This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching, and good night.
